s.t: Devendra Banhart set it in an alternative universe where the Catholic saint Hildegard von Bingen escapes the confines of her life to become a VJ for MTV.
s.src: Paste: Listen to Devendra Banhart’s new song “Für Hildegard von Bingen” (8 January 2013)
s.q: In a press release, Banhart explained that the song takes place in an alternative universe where the real-life female Catholic saint, referenced in the title, escapes the confinements of her life to become a VJ for MTV.

s.t: Devendra Banhart and Noah Georgeson recorded it at Banhart’s Los Angeles home on a vintage Tascam used for early hip-hop, curious how his songs would sound on rap equipment.
s.q: Banhart co-produced the album with his guitarist, Noah Georgeson, in his then-home in Los Angeles (Banhart has since moved to New York). The two played almost all of the instruments themselves and used a vintage Tascam recorder. "A lot of early hip-hop had been made on [the Tascam]," Banhart said in a statement. "And knowing my songs are not hip-hop whatsoever, we thought it would be interesting to see how these kinds of songs would sound on equipment that was used to record our favourite rap."

s.t: In Isaiah Seret and Devendra Banhart’s video for it, a nun secretly worships the city’s art world behind the head priest’s back and fantasises about singing with Klaus Nomi.
s.src: Stereogum: Devendra Banhart – “Für Hildegard Von Bingen” Video (29 October 2013)
s.q: The story follows a nun who secretly worships the art world of the city behind the back of the head priest. Her fantasies come to life with superimposed images of her singing with Klaus Nomi, certainly one of the saints of downtown New York in the '70s. It's an exquisite looking video, directed by Isaiah Seret and Banhart.

s.t: Devendra Banhart wrote it to celebrate Hildegard von Bingen as a medieval feminist who had the strength to say ‘Yes we are equal’ when few feminists were around.
s.src: SPIN: Devendra Banhart Riffs on Britpop, Drag, and German Mystics (7 March 2013)
s.q: She’s a fabulous composer but also she’s a medieval feminist — when there weren’t that many feminists around. For somebody to have the strength to say, ‘Yes we are equal, and also , I’m a composer, a pedagogue, a herbalist.’ These are revolutionary things even today, but imagine then. She’s certainly somebody that deserves celebration, so this is a song for her.

f.t: At nine he sang his family his first song, ‘We’re All Going to Die’, written after learning what plastic surgery was. Horrified, they told him never to do it again.
f.src: NPR: Devendra Banhart On The Moment He Became A Songwriter (15 October 2016)
f.q: And their response, their reaction, was never do that again. Never do that again. They were horrified. It was - I mean, I can't blame them. It was a song called "We're All Going To Die." I had just been told what plastic surgery was.

f.t: Aged eight, wanting to sing like Axl Rose and Kurt Cobain, he put on one of his mother’s dresses while nobody was around and suddenly found he could sing.
f.src: SPIN: Devendra Banhart Riffs on Britpop, Drag, and German Mystics (7 March 2013)
f.q: I was eight years old and I wanted to sing like those guys — Axl Rose and Kurt Cobain — but I was an eight-year-old boy so I couldn’t, my voice didn’t sound like that. So one day no one was around and I put on one of my mom’s dresses. I combed my hair, and I was this woman. Suddenly I had permission, I could sing.

f.t: When his father brought home a David Byrne compilation of Brazilian music, Caetano Veloso’s ‘O Leãozinho’ on it told him what he wanted to do with his life.
f.src: Sounds and Colours: When I Think of Venezuela I Think of My Mother: An Interview with Devendra Banhart (31 October 2019)
f.q: my dad brought home this compilation that was called Beleza Tropical that David Byrne put together on Luaka Bop ... the main thing that really blew my mind was Caetano and it was “O Leaozinho” the song. ... when I hear Caetano’s “Leaozinho” I knew, that’s it, I just want to do this, that’s exactly what I want to do.

f.t: His first name was suggested by the Indian religious leader Prem Rawat, whom his parents followed; his middle name, Obi, comes from Obi-Wan Kenobi in Star Wars.
f.q: The name "Devendra"—which is a synonym for the Hindu god Indra—was suggested by the Indian religious leader Prem Rawat, whom Banhart's parents followed. Banhart's middle name was derived from the Star Wars character Obi-Wan Kenobi.

f.t: His first ever show was in a church at a gay wedding, where he sang Elvis Presley’s ‘Love Me Tender’ and the hymn ‘How Great Thou Art’.
f.q: He played his first musical show in a church at a gay wedding, performing Elvis Presley's "Love Me Tender" and the hymn "How Great Thou Art".

nf.t: A 12th-century Christian mystic, reimagined as an MTV VJ.
nf.q: thankfully, the synths and drum machines make palatably whimsical a two-part reimagining of 12th-century Christian mystic Hildegard Von Bingen as an MTV VJ.
